name: GA-10
label: Safe R

key_factors: Houston Gaines has a large fundraising and outside-spending edge; Pam Delancy has raised almost nothing
Open seat after Mike Collins retired to run for Senate
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
model.rationale: This is an open seat in a district that leans Republican by about eleven points, and the Republican nominee holds a massive financial advantage with over $2.3 million raised and outside support while the Democrat has raised roughly $23,000. Markets price a Republican win near 95%, so the forecast sits slightly beyond the fundamentals-based baseline but well short of Safe R given the lack of polls and the open-seat uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Democrat competitive, or a surprise in the Republican primary outcome, would be the main signal to move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Mike Collins (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Georgia's 10th District is an open seat after Republican Mike Collins left to run for Senate. The district leans Republican by about eleven points, and the Republican nominee, Houston Gaines, has built a commanding financial position with $2.3 million raised and roughly $1.5 million in outside support. Democrat Pam Delancy has raised about $23,000 with no outside spending, leaving her badly outmatched in resources.

Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 95%, and no expert raters or public polls cover the race. The forecast rests on the district's partisan lean and the money gap, pointing to a likely Republican hold with a margin in the mid-teens, though the open seat and absence of polling add some uncertainty.
